newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korean stocks end higher despite strikes.
newsitem.headline: South Korean stocks end higher despite strikes.

text.p: Seoul stocks rose by the end of Friday's limited session on a rebound after sharp falls during the last trading days of 1996, brokers said.
Despite a call for a resumption of industrial action by the Korean Confederation of Trade Unions, investors felt labour unrest was diminishing after the New Year holidays, they added.
The composite stock index rose 2.57 points to 653.79 from last year's close of 651.22.
This was 11.9 points higher from Friday's opening level of 641.89.
"At the end of last year, there was a sharp fall in the index, and today, there was a rebound due to that," said Park Sang-oon, a broker at Seoul Securities.
The index opening figure had been revised downward after taking into account companies that balance their books in December and firms that have gone ex-dividend as of December 31.
"Sentiment toward blue chips and construction firms improved because investors expect the government to boost the economy ahead of this year's elections," said Jay Kwon of Hanwha Securities.
POSCO gained 2,700 won to 38,300, while KEPCO jumped 1,500 won to 25,900 in active trading.
Brokers said large infrastructure projects were expected to be launched to help raise the economy. Hyundai Engineering rose 1,500 won to 20,800, and Chunggu Construction climbed 1,600 to 22,200.
On Friday, the bourse was open for trading from 11.00 a.m. (0200 GMT) - 1.00 p.m. (0400 GMT).
The bourse had been hit by strikes after the ruling New Korea Party rammed a bill revising labour legislation through parliament on December 26.
